span.p: HIERARCHICAL PAIR TRACK - 3 LEVELS

span.p:
LEVEL 1 - DENSE coarse map at b=16
0.396 pct of dense cost
at L=4096 this is only 65k entries
NO recall loss: it is genuinely dense

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
LEVEL 2 - refine occupied b=16 blocks to b=4
0.460 pct of dense cost

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
LEVEL 3 - refine occupied b=4 blocks to pairs
1.346 pct of dense cost
mean c 17.14 | p99 19.13 | MAX 21.14
target_c = 24 (20 was BREACHED)

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: THE FIX - CONTACTS ARE CLUSTERED, NOT LOCAL

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Helical stems are contiguous anti-diagonal runs,
so contacts occupy very FEW BLOCKS
even when spread along the sequence.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
OCCUPANCY FALLS AS CHAINS GET LONGER
=> the mechanism gets MORE effective exactly
where the flat design failed

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: BANDED FALLBACK ALSO FAILS - MEASURED

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
fraction of contacts within |i-j| <= band, L 1500-3000:
band 32: 0.350 | band 64: 0.479 | band 128: 0.597
band 256: 0.706 | band 512: 0.812

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
median contact separation 78 nt with a long tail.
Even a +/-512 band misses 19 pct.

span.p:
Flat top-K, K = 32L, sequence-only proposer
recall of true 3D contacts:

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: L 32-100: 0.980 recall ... but K = 59 pct of dense

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: L 500-1200: 0.200 recall = ONE CONTACT IN FIVE

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
RANDOM scorer gets 0.746 mean recall at c=32
because short chains dominate the average.
The flat proposer is barely above chance.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
TOTAL 2.202 pct of dense
vs flat top-K: 1.118 pct of dense
but only ~20 pct recall.
~2x the cost buys a 100 pct recall CEILING
instead of a hard 20 pct floor.
NOTE: max c measured on derivatives that
under-represent modified residues 40x.
24 is interim; re-derive on raw PDB.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY IT IS EASIER TO LEARN
Deciding whether a 16x16 block contains ANY contact
aggregates 256 pair-decisions into one.
The model ranks 32k blocks, not 4.1M pairs.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
STILL UNPROVEN
Measurements show the INFORMATION is there and the
cost is affordable. They do NOT show a trained model
will find the occupied blocks.
External evidence: ERNIE-RNA reaches Top-L/1 = 0.68
zero-shot from attention alone.
Block-detection recall MUST be reported per level.
